title: Reading a rockfall's age from its lichens
bodyMd: A rockfall leaves behind boulders whose exposed faces begin as bare stone. Geologist Priya Raman uses the lichens that later colonise those faces as a rough clock: the map lichen *Rhizocarpon* spreads outward at a slow and fairly steady rate, so the widest lichen on a boulder gives a minimum age for the fall that exposed it. Raman measured lichens on boulders below a Norwegian cliff whose collapses are dated in parish registers. For falls less than about 300 years old, lichen diameter tracked the recorded dates closely. Beyond that, growth had slowed so much that her estimates bunched together, blurring events a century or more apart.
accessibilityText: A short science passage. A rockfall leaves boulders with bare exposed stone faces. Geologist Priya Raman uses lichens as a clock: the map lichen Rhizocarpon grows outward slowly and steadily, so the widest lichen on a boulder gives a minimum age for the rockfall. Raman measured lichens on boulders below a Norwegian cliff whose collapse dates appear in parish registers. For falls less than about 300 years old, lichen diameter matched the recorded dates closely. For older falls, lichen growth had slowed so much that her age estimates bunched together and could not separate events a century or more apart.

provenance.notes: Original passage written for this item bank. The geologist, the Norwegian site and the 300-year figure are invented; lichenometry is described only in general terms and no published text was consulted or adapted.
